To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the impact of GNSS spoofings on the integrated navigation systems is dependent on the type of spoofing attack and the time duration of the spoofing attack.
the integrated navigation system is more vulnerable to spoofing attacks when the inertial sensors are not well calibrated and the inertial sensor bias is not estimated.

the Kalman filter’s innovation sequence is an effective indicator for detecting spoofing attacks, and that the Kalman gain and the inertial sensor bias estimates are effective indicators for mitigating spoofing attacks.

the following three questions. (1) How does the integrated navigation system respond to different kinds of GNSS spoofings? (2) How do we detect spoofings based on the behavior of the integrated navigation systems? and (3) How do we mitigate spoofings?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the impact of the spoofing attack is dependent on the spoofed trajectory’s characteristics, the navigation system configuration, and the navigation system’s initial conditions, and it is also dependent on the navigation system’s Kalman filter’s design and tuning parameters.
the Kalman filter error covariance and innovation sequence can be utilized for detecting the spoofing attacks, while the inertial sensor bias can be used for spoofing mitigation.

GNSS spoofing attack is a serious threat to the integrity of the integrated navigation, and the integrated navigation system can be used to detect the spoofing attacks and mitigate the impact on the navigation performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Kalman filter’s innovation sequence is the most sensitive metric in detecting GNSS spoofing.

the integrated navigation system is vulnerable to both unsynchronized and coordinated spoofing attacks, and that the Kalman filter’s innovations are a promising spoofing detection metric for both types of spoofing attacks.

, the integrated navigation system can be used to detect the spoofing attack by monitoring the error covariance matrix of the Kalman filter and the innovation sequence of the integrated navigation filter.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the presence of spoofing attacks, the integrated navigation system will not be able to detect the attacks, and the inertial sensor bias will be overestimated, which will lead to a biased navigation solution.
the Kalman filter is able to detect and mitigate the impact of unsynchronized spoofing attacks, while it is unable to detect and mitigate synchronized spoofing attacks.

the impact of spoofing attacks on integrated navigation systems is not as straightforward as one would think and it is important to consider the system’s dynamics and the specific characteristics of the spoofing attack in order to make an accurate prediction of the system’s behavior.
